results.summary: This design adds the values of the eight input switches and displays the single-digit sum on a 7-segment display. If the sum exceeds 9, the display is blanked, so only sums from 0 to 9 are shown. It is intended as a simple educational demonstration of combinational logic and arithmetic. External hardware required is a single 7-segment display; no on-chip memory or clock is used.

This project uses simple logic gates (NOT, NAND, OR) to drive a 7-segment display so that it shows the letter 'J'. The input switches set the pattern, and according to the documentation, turning on switches 1, 4, 5, 6, and 8 (with 2, 3, and 7 off) produces the desired output. The design is a Wokwi-based educational exercise, likely created as a class project. It requires an external 7-segment display and has minimal documentation beyond the switch settings.

This design uses an AND gate and a NAND gate to control a 7-segment display, changing the displayed number between 1 and 5 when the second switch is toggled. The documentation is minimal and the exact mapping of inputs to segments is not fully explained. It is a simple educational project built in Wokwi. Required external hardware is a 7-segment display.

This project implements several basic logic gates: two AND gates, two NAND gates, two OR gates, and one NOT gate, with inputs a through h and corresponding outputs. The documentation includes a truth table for the AND, NAND, OR, and NOT functions, but it is unclear how the multiple outputs for each gate type are derived. It is a straightforward educational design for testing gate behavior. No external hardware is specified beyond the switches and output indicators.

This design connects input switches through NOT and AND gates to drive the segments of a 7-segment display. The documentation is poorly written and vague, but it indicates that each switch controls a specific segment or combination, with some segments requiring multiple switches. It is a simple educational project, likely for learning basic logic and display driving. External hardware includes resistors, pushbuttons, a 7-segment display, and a slide switch.

This project implements a NOT gate on input 1 and an AND gate on inputs 5 and 6, with corresponding outputs, and also includes a clock divider as mentioned in the one-line description. The documentation provides a specific sequence of switch settings to test the design, but it is unclear how the clock divider is implemented or connected. It appears to be a basic educational test design. No external hardware is listed.

This design uses OR, AND, and NAND gates to combine inputs and produce outputs, as described in the documentation. The exact gate connections are not fully specified, but the project is a simple logic gate test. It is likely an educational exercise built in Wokwi. No external hardware is required.

This project implements AND, NAND, and NOT gates, as well as an SR latch built from two NOR gates with feedback. The documentation provides detailed instructions for testing, including power setup, verifying basic gates, and testing the latch behavior. It is an educational design intended to demonstrate combinational and sequential logic. External hardware includes momentary pushbuttons, pull-up resistors, LEDs or a 7-segment display, and a breadboard with a regulated supply.

This design is intended to display the initials of the user's name using a basic LCD. The documentation is very minimal and mentions switches, LEDs, and an LCD, but the exact operation and pin usage are unclear. It is a Wokwi-based educational project. The external hardware required is an LED display or LCD, but the description is too vague to determine the specifics.

This project uses XOR and NOT gates to process inputs a through h and produce outputs, aiming to display a pattern resembling the Greek letter lambda. The documentation is extremely sparse and includes placeholder text, making it difficult to understand the exact gate connections or the intended display. It is an educational design built in Wokwi. No external hardware is specified.
